disagreements.topic: FY28 revenue base (and the round-1 supervisor's own figure)
disagreements.positions: Agent 1 uses FY28 ~$3.8-3.9B (+55%) and agent 2 ~$3.7-3.8B, both following the round-1 supervisor's '$3.8-3.9B implied by consensus EPS'. Agents 3 and 5 moved only part way, to $3.7B (+48%) and $3.65B (+46%). Agent 4 uses +50-55%.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus (StockAnalysis read 2026-10-26; now cited to 24/7 Wall St [src 55] and TIKR [src 54]) shows next-year (FY28) revenue $3.88B (+55% on FY27 $2.50B) and EPS $9.71, whose basis (GAAP or non-GAAP) neither source states, so no net margin is inferred from it and it enters no number; Zacks' FY28 EPS is $8.30 [src 28] on a basis below company non-GAAP. The $3.69B FY28 / $4.80B FY29 figures this round first used could not be verified and are dropped, and no public FY29 consensus was found. On $3.88B, the round-1 supervisor's $3.8-3.9B was right: agents 1 and 2 are on consensus and agents 3 and 5 ($3.7B, $3.65B) are ~5-6% below it. What matters at the horizon is NTM revenue at Sep-2027 (H2 FY28 + H1 FY29), which cannot be pinned to a public consensus. Net effect on the mean fair value is small.
disagreements.evidence: Consensus as read 2026-10-26 on StockAnalysis (FY27 $2.50B / EPS $6.31; FY28 $3.88B / EPS $9.71); the page as served on 2026-11-16 shows an older vintage, so the figures are now cited to 24/7 Wall St 2026-11-10 (FY27 $2.50B, EPS $6.3093; FY28 EPS $9.7121) [src 55] and TIKR (FY28 revenue $3.88B) [src 54]; neither states the EPS basis. 24/7 Wall St (FY28 EPS $8.69 -> $9.70 in 90 days, 14 up-revisions).

disagreements.topic: NTM EPS weighting at the horizon (agent 5)
disagreements.positions: Agent 5 builds Sep-2027 NTM EPS as 0.7 x FY28 + 0.3 x FY29 and states ~$9.90; on its own FY28 $8.90 and FY29 $11.80 that weighting gives $9.77 (0.7 x 8.90 + 0.3 x 11.80), and its $238 P/E leg is 24 x the stated $9.90. Agents 1, 2 and 4 use ~$10.0-10.4 and agent 3 uses $11.3.
disagreements.resolution: Credo's fiscal year ends around 1 May, so on 2027-09-25 Q1 FY28 has been reported and the NTM window is Q3-Q4 FY28 plus Q1-Q2 FY29, about 50/50 FY28/FY29. On agent 5's own FY28 $8.90 and FY29 $11.80, NTM EPS is ~$10.35 (0.5 x 8.90 + 0.5 x 11.80), not $9.77 (its 0.7/0.3 weighting) or the ~$9.90 it states. At its 24x, its P/E leg becomes ~$248 (from $238), which lifts its blend by ~$4-5. No consensus NTM EPS is computed: the FY28 consensus EPS sources found do not state their basis and no public FY29 consensus was found. Every agent except agent 3 haircuts consensus 7-10% in its base case and also carries a separate 25-33% bear scenario, which partly double-counts the same concentration and competition risk.
disagreements.evidence: Q1 FY27 reported 2026-09-01 for the quarter ended ~Aug 1; StockAnalysis FY28 EPS $9.71 (read 2026-10-26).

disagreements.positions: Agent 4 applies 9x NTM sales ($184). Agents 2, 3 and 5 use 11-11.5x and agent 1 uses 10x ($212-240).
disagreements.resolution: At management's FY27 non-GAAP net-margin outlook of ~50% [src 22], agent 4's own 22x P/E leg is equivalent to ~11x sales. A 9x sales multiple implies ~18x earnings, so the two legs contradict each other. At 11x on its own $4.0B NTM revenue plus $1.8B cash over 205M shares, the leg is ~$223, which lifts agent 4's blend from $216 to ~$226. The multiple regime is compressing (Mizuho cut its target to $245 from $290 on lower peer multiples), so I do not push anyone above 11.5x.
disagreements.evidence: Agent 4 method inputs; Investing.com on the Mizuho note; management's FY27 non-GAAP net-margin outlook 'in the vicinity of 50%' [src 22].

disagreements.resolution: Not settled by search, so I keep the mean (~21%). The concentration is real: end customers are 33% and 28% and one direct customer is 43% of revenue and 57% of receivables, and the three-month crash was driven by concentration fears, not by fundamentals. The funding backdrop cuts both ways. S&P sees six hyperscalers spending ~$1.3T in 2027, but only Microsoft is forecast to be free-cash-flow positive, so a 2027 digestion is a live risk. My searches did not confirm a documented Marvell share win at Amazon for 1.6T AECs.
disagreements.evidence: 24/7 Wall St crash analysis; Motley Fool on 2027 hyperscaler capex and FCF.

disagreements.positions: Agent 5 dates Q2 FY27 earnings to 2026-12-02 while the others say 'early December'. Agent 5 also cites a '$210.12 close on 2026-09-26'.
disagreements.resolution: Q2 FY27 earnings are not yet scheduled: TipRanks estimates 2026-12-01 after the close and marks it not confirmed; TIKR says 'early December'. 2026-09-26 was a Saturday, so there was no close that day. The Trefis piece dated 9/26 describes the 9/25 close of $210.97, and the brief's anchor is right. Update 2026-11-23: Credo's 2026-11-11 release schedules the Q2 FY27 call for Tuesday, December 1, 2026, 2:00 p.m. PT [src 103].
disagreements.evidence: TipRanks earnings calendar (estimated, not confirmed) [src 5]; TIKR [src 54]; Trefis 9-day/41% article dated 2026-09-26.

drivers.source: Big-4 capex path: the project's shared path from the NVDA 2026-11-09 round [src 35] (CY2025 $410.0B; CY2026 $750.70B on the shared path's quarter basis: H1 CY2026 on its scaled cash basis $321.4B (XBRL cash PP&E x 1.0903) + Q3 $207.41B as reported + Q4 $221.88B (each company's 2026 guide less its 9-month spend) [src 35]; the Q3 calls' 2026 guides themselves sum to $730.1B on the companies' own basis (Microsoft ~$170B, Alphabet $195-205B, Amazon ~$220B, Meta $135-145B [src 36, 37, 38, 39]), and the NVDA set states both figures; CY2027 $1,013.88B and CY2028 $1,359.36B per company from the business its capacity serves in that round). From the 2026-11-23 update: the NVDA 2026-11-17 print round's gate-clean shared path [src 101]: CY2026 $750.70B unchanged, CY2027 $1,009.45B, CY2028 $1,305.26B, rebuilt per company on Kilian's capacity-driver method from the Q3 CY2026 calls (Amazon capex grown with AWS, which CEO Andy Jassy says 'can grow north of 40% in each of 2027 and in 2028'; Alphabet with Google Cloud backlog conversion, 'just over 55%' of $561B 'over the next 24 months' (CFO Anat Ashkenazi); Microsoft with the commercial RPO due in 12 months, 'up 29%' (CFO Amy Hood); Meta 2027 at the S&P Global revenue consensus +21.70% [src 102] at its H2-2026 capex/revenue, and Meta CY2028 at its CY2027 level, Kilian's NVDA card 2026-11-18, because Meta gives nothing for 2028 (CFO Susan Li: nothing more quantitative until the Q4 call) [src 36, 37, 38, 39, 101, 102]); the old path is kept as src 35. The NVDA 2026-11-23 round is in progress and not used. Replacing the 10-23 project build (733/1,080/1,330 [src 23]), x a copper attach of 0.60% of capex (estimate). No citable copper TAM: Credo's FY2026 10-K has no market-opportunity figure [src 12]; management calls ALC, scale-up and OmniConnect 'multibillion dollar' opportunities without a copper figure [src 22].
drivers.derivation: PLAIN READING (Kilian 2026-11-16 16:15Z): copper revenue grows with Big-4 capex; this is not a market share. The 0.60% attach is a scaling device with no source: share is calibrated to Credo's actual copper revenue, so the attach level cancels and copper revenue = Q1 FY27 copper x capex growth x (1 - MaxLinear loss). No current public AEC market forecast was found: LightCounting's December 2023 newsletter put AOC, DAC and AEC sales at $2.8B by 2028 (stale, src 97); its December 2025 update is a paid report ($5,995, no figures on the public page, src 98), and 650 Group's AEC report publishes no figure in its launch release (src 99). Update 2026-11-13 (tape-hold read-through, 2026-11-16): capex path moved to the shared NVDA 11-09 hs_capex so every AI-capex name reads one path. TAM = Big-4 capex x 0.60%: CY2025 410 x 0.006 = $2.46B; CY2026 750.70 x 0.006 = $4.504B; CY2027 1,013.88 x 0.006 = $6.083B; CY2028 1,359.36 x 0.006 = $8.156B (was 4.398 / 6.48 / 7.98). Update 2026-11-23: the shared path moves to the NVDA 2026-11-17 print round's hs_capex [src 101] (per-company capacity build; Meta CY2028 199.8 = its CY2027 level, Kilian's NVDA card; the 11-09 path had Meta 2028 on its 2027 revenue growth a second year, refused there as a carried rate): CY2027 1,009.45 x 0.006 = $6.0567B, CY2028 1,305.26 x 0.006 = $7.8316B (was $6.083B / $8.156B); CY2026 750.70 unchanged. The 0.60% attach is a calibration: it makes Credo's FY2026 copper revenue (~$1,275M, see segment base) ~52% of the TAM; MaxLinear's CEO estimated that Credo accounts for 93% to 99% of the AEC cable market (Stocktwits' paraphrase of the call [src 40]), and Marvell retimers are the most widely adopted by AEC integrators [src 43], so Credo's share of the wider copper wallet (AECs plus retimers/PHYs) is below its AEC share. Cross-check: LightCounting puts optics sales to the top five cloud providers at 2.7% of their capex in 2025 (Lightwave 2026-03-10 on the 'Optics for AI Clusters' report [src 33]), so copper at 0.6% is ~1/5 of the optics spend (0.6 / 2.7 = 0.22). The attach level cancels in revenue (copper_share is calibrated to it); what moves value is the capex growth and the share trend. Fiscal/calendar alignment: Credo's FY n runs May n-1 to April n (FY2026 ended 2026-05-02), so 8 of its 12 months fall in CY n-1; FY n is paired with CY n-1 (FY26 = CY2025, FY27 = CY2026, FY28 = CY2027, FY29 = CY2028), (calendar arithmetic; the pairing is the nearest calendar year, not a stated lead). Variant view: attach rising with AEC penetration at 1.6T and scale-up (e.g. 0.6% -> 0.7% by CY2028) would lift FY29 copper ~17% at the same share; Street CY2027 Big-4 consensus $934.5B (IO Fund [src 56]) to $1,029.1B (S&P Global [src 8]), ~$0.98T midpoint (adhoc/nvda_customer_capex.md [src 23]), with Goldman Sachs +12% for 2028 [src 114]: FY28 TAM $5.88B, FY29 $6.59B, research target (12m) -7.76% (carded); Goldman Sachs' full path (+54% 2027, +12% 2028 [src 114]) on the shared CY2026 $750.70B: $1,156.1B / $1,294.8B, FY28 TAM $6.937B, FY29 $7.769B, +4.90%; Morgan Stanley bars +8.72% (relay of the 2026-11-08 note; the bars rest on the NVDA gate's 2026-11-12 read of the relay page, the owner confirmed the note on 2026-11-10; it could not be re-opened on 2026-11-17; alternative only, not booked) and attach rising to 0.70% +10.03% (both carded); the project capex file's low / high Big-4 scenarios -20.95% / +26.89% (carded); SemiAnalysis's 2026-11-13 volume cut, platform-weighted net of the moratorium -13.60% to all-platform gross -18.19% (carded) (engine, 2026-11-23 set, research target (12m) 209.34). QUARTERS (2026-10-29): Each quarter carries its fiscal year's calendar-year level (Big-4 capex x 0.60%); no source gives a quarterly TAM, so the within-year shape sits in copper_share (built from the shared path's quarters since the 2026-11-16 gate fix). Actual quarters carry the same estimate (not a filed figure).

drivers.label: Copper revenue / copper scaling base (calibrated to Credo's copper revenue; not a market share)
drivers.source: Base: FY2026 copper revenue ~$1,275.1M (estimate, segment base row) / CY2025 copper TAM $2.46B = 51.8%. Forecast quarters (gate fix 2026-11-16, bottom-up): copper revenue grows from the Q1 FY27 level with the shared Big-4 capex path [src 35] (Q1-Q2 CY2029, beyond the path: Dell'Oro's July 2026 forecast has worldwide data-center capex above $3 trillion by 2030 with the Top 4 US hyperscalers about half [src 67], which on the shared CY2028 gives +5.0% a year for CY2029-30; estimate), less a MaxLinear 1.6T AEC share loss: MaxLinear targets 20-30% of the 1.6T AEC market 'over the next couple of years', selling silicon to cable makers, initial focus 'one or two large U.S. data centers' [src 40]; initial 1.6T revenue in 2027, stronger volumes in 2028 [src 41]; 1.6T ~56% of 2027 pluggable optical transceiver revenue (TrendForce [src 42]; used as the proxy for the 1.6T share of AEC revenue in Q1 FY28; held at 56% for FY28-29: HSBC has 3.2T at ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 [src 66, a relay of a non-public note], so the 1.6T-only share need not keep rising; no source gives a 2028-29 1.6T revenue share); AEC share of copper revenue 0.90 (estimate, bounded below at ~88% by the FY26 10-K's 'contributed over 99% of the increase in revenue' [src 12; phrase located by EDGAR full-text search, src 51] and the FY25 10-K revenue split and its 'AEC products, which contributed over 95% of the increase in product sales' [src 30; phrase located by EDGAR full-text search, src 60], arithmetic in the derivation). Credo sells to 'hyperscalers, Neoclouds, OEMs, ODMs, CMs and optical module manufacturers' [src 12].
drivers.derivation: PLAIN READING (Kilian 2026-11-16 16:15Z): copper revenue grows with Big-4 capex; this is not a market share. The 0.60% attach is a scaling device with no source: share is calibrated to Credo's actual copper revenue, so the attach level cancels and copper revenue = Q1 FY27 copper x capex growth x (1 - MaxLinear loss). No current public AEC market forecast was found: LightCounting's December 2023 newsletter put AOC, DAC and AEC sales at $2.8B by 2028 (stale, src 97); its December 2025 update is a paid report ($5,995, no figures on the public page, src 98), and 650 Group's AEC report publishes no figure in its launch release (src 99). Gate fix 2026-11-16 (replaces the FY27 share taken from the >85% growth guide and consensus, and the H2 quarters shaped to them): copper_q = Q1 FY27 copper 444 (fifth gate fix: 479.0 less optical 35.0 within the 10-Q's 'over 90%' AEC cap [src 11]; was 424 on optical 55) x (Big-4 capex in the paired calendar quarter / capex in Q3 CY2026) x (1 - MaxLinear loss_q). Pairing (estimate, confidence low): each Credo quarter is paired with the calendar quarter after the one it overlaps most (Q1 FY27 May-Jul 2026 with Q3 CY2026, ... Q2 FY29 with Q4 CY2028, Q4 FY29 with Q2 CY2029), because part of Credo's revenue is billed to ODMs, CMs and module makers [src 12] before the finished racks reach the hyperscalers' capex. The lead is our estimate (confidence low): no source states it or sizes it; the no-lead (same-quarter) pairing is sized in judgment_alternatives (+6.41% (engine, 2026-11-23 set, research target (12m) 209.34)) and carded. Shared path quarters (from 2026-11-23 the NVDA 2026-11-17 round's hs_capex [src 101]; its quarters split each calendar year at one q/q rate because no Big-4 company gives a 2027-28 cadence): Q3 CY2026 207.41, Q4 221.88, CY2027 233.45 / 245.63 / 258.44 / 271.93, CY2028 292.13 / 313.82 / 337.14 / 362.18 ($B) (was 233.85 / 246.47 / 259.77 / 273.79 and 297.98 / 324.30 / 352.95 / 384.13 on the NVDA 11-09 path [src 35]). Q1-Q2 CY2029 (fourth gate fix; replaces +12% carried from Goldman Sachs' 2028 rate, which no 2029 source supported): the shared path ends at CY2028; Dell'Oro's July 2026 forecast puts worldwide data-center capex above $3 trillion by 2030 with the Top 4 US hyperscalers about half [src 67], so ~$1,500B for the Top 4 in 2030; CY2029 is read halfway (geometric) between the shared CY2028 and that 2030 level: on the NVDA 11-17 path's CY2028 $1,305.26B, sqrt(1,305.26 x 1,500) = $1,399.2B (was $1,428.0B on the 11-09 path's $1,359.36B) (estimate, confidence low: Dell'Oro's series is data-center capex, the shared path is total capex; flagged for Kilian as a reading between a path year and an outside 2030 figure), spread at a constant quarterly rate from Q4 CY2028 (-1.38% a quarter: 357.16 / 352.21; was -2.91%, 372.95 / 362.10; a +5% year lands below four quarters at the Q4 CY2028 exit because CY2028 ramps through the year); Goldman Sachs' +12% carried (+0.01%), flat at Q4 CY2028 (+0.01%) and +17% (+0.01%) alternatives sized (engine, 2026-11-23 set, research target (12m) 209.34). Copper before dc_mor (2026-11-23, NVDA 11-17 path): Q2 FY27 475.0, Q3 499.7, Q4 525.8 (FY27 $1,944.5M); FY28 541.6 / 557.7 / 586.0 / 615.4 ($2,300.6M); FY29 645.9 / 677.6 / 668.2 / 659.0 ($2,650.8M) (was Q3-Q4 FY27 500.6 / 527.6, FY27 $1,947.2M; FY28 544.4 / 561.5 / 597.7 / 635.9 = $2,339.5M; FY29 676.2 / 718.7 / 697.8 / 677.5 = $2,770.2M). share_q = copper_q x 4 / (year TAM x 1000). MaxLinear loss_q = AEC share of copper 0.90 x 1.6T share of AEC revenue (56% from TrendForce's 2027 pluggable optical mix [src 42], used as a proxy for AECs, held through FY29 (fourth gate fix; was +2pt a quarter to 70%, which no source supported): HSBC has 3.2T at ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 [src 66, a relay of a non-public note], so 1.6T alone need not keep rising after 2027; no source gives a 2028-29 1.6T revenue share; the old rise to 70%, which reads MaxLinear as contesting 3.2T AECs too, is sized at -1.18%) x MaxLinear share of 1.6T AEC (linear ramp from Q1 FY28, first revenue 2027 [src 41], to the 25% midpoint of its 20-30% target by Q2 FY29, two years after the call (Quartr dates it 23 Oct 2026 [src 41]; Stocktwits write-up 2026-10-23 [src 40]), then held): FY28 2.1% / 4.2% / 6.3% / 8.4%, FY29 10.5% / 12.6% / 12.6% / 12.6%. AEC share of copper 0.90 (estimate, confidence medium): the FY26 10-K says the AEC ramp 'contributed over 99% of the increase in revenue' [src 12, 51], so FY26 non-AEC revenue rose by less than 1% x 898.3 = $9.0M. FY25 non-AEC revenue is at most IP licensing $12.5M + engineering services $12.1M + non-AEC product sales [src 30] (both amounts checked 2026-11-17 by EDGAR full-text search, 10-K forms, CIK 1807794: 'engineering services' with '12.1 million' and 'IP license' with '12.5' hit only the FY25 10-K, acc 0001628280-25-033813, crdo-20250503.htm, and the FY24 10-K, acc 0001628280-24-029629); the FY25 10-K says 'AEC products, which contributed over 95% of the increase in product sales' (phrase confirmed by EDGAR full-text search: among 10-Ks the only hit is the FY25 10-K; four 10-Qs also carry it [src 60]), so even if every FY24 product dollar was non-AEC (FY24 revenue $193.0M less 15% IP = $164.1M) non-AEC product sales were at most 164.1 + 5% x (412.2 - 164.1) = $176.5M, FY25 non-AEC at most $201.1M and FY26 at most $210.1M; less optical ~$60M leaves at most $150.1M of non-AEC copper, so AECs are at least 1,125.0 / 1,275.1 = 88.2% of FY26 copper (worst case; arithmetic, not a stated share). 0.90 sits just above that bound (moderately conservative: a higher AEC share means a larger MaxLinear loss). Why book the loss (base case moderately conservative, Kilian 2026-11-10): a named competitor gave a share target on its call and dates its revenue; Marvell's retimer chips are 'the most widely adopted by AEC system integrators (more than Broadcom's)' [src 43]. Against: MaxLinear sells silicon, not cables, the target is its own, it focuses on one or two large US data centers, and its CEO estimated Credo at 93% to 99% of the AEC cable market (Stocktwits paraphrase [src 40]); management says 'AECs remain our largest business and continues to grow', it has 'deep relationships with 5 hyperscalers', sees 'increased AEC penetration' within existing customers, and its fourth 10% customer in Q1 FY27 was a returning former 10% customer [src 22]; it also expects 'additional customer ramps during fiscal 27 across both 800-gig and 1.6T' [src 22], which this build does not size (upside). Cross-checks only (not inputs): Q2 FY27 total 531.6 vs the $525-535M guide [src 10] (+0.3% on the midpoint); FY27 total $2,370.1M (+77.5%; was $2,372.7M, +77.7%, before the 2026-11-23 capex-path update) vs the '>85%' guide [src 22] and the Zacks $2.50B consensus [src 28]. Actual quarters: copper = reported revenue (8-K Ex-99.1 releases (acc 0001807794-25-000018, 0001628280-25-054428, 0001628280-26-013205, 0001628280-26-039474): 223.1 / 268.0 / 407.0 / 437.0; Q1 FY27 8-K Ex-99.1 acc 0001628280-26-059795 / 10-Q acc 0001628280-26-060111: 479.0) less estimated optical (10 / 12 / 17 / 21; Q1 FY27 35.0, capped by the 10-Q's 'over 90%' AEC share of the y/y rise [src 11]). Seasonality: none usable; FY25 quarter shares 13.7/16.5/30.9/38.9% (Q1 FY25 59.8 = FY25 436.8 [F2] - 72.0 - 135.0 - 170.0) and FY26 16.7/20.1/30.5/32.7% are the ramp, not a calendar pattern. ALC is placed in optical, OmniConnect gearboxes (electrical, first revenue FY28 [src 22]) here. Bear: dual-sourcing at the top customer is carried by top_customer_pct, not here.

drivers.label: Non-GAAP gross margin, copper (AECs, electrical ICs, SerDes IP)
drivers.source: Not disclosed by line. Base solved from the FY2026 blended non-GAAP gross margin 68.14% ($909.8M / $1,335.1M, Q4 FY26 release reconciliation [src 13]) with optical at 65% and 4.49% of revenue. Reported blended non-GAAP GM 67.6% / 67.7% / 68.6% / 68.3% (FY26 quarters [src 16, 15, 14, 13]) and 68.0% (Q1 FY27 [src 10]); FY27 blended guide 'broadly consistent with fiscal year 26 levels' and Q2 67-69% [src 22, 10]. FY28-29 price pressure: Marvell's retimers 'typically priced 15-20% below Credo's when supplied to third-party buyers' (Semi Fundamental [src 43]; the author attributes it to secondhand channel feedback, 'we heard', not a measured price); MaxLinear sells AEC silicon to cable makers, initial focus 'one or two large U.S. data centers' [src 40]; 1.6T ~56% of 2027 pluggable optical transceiver revenue [src 42] (proxy for the AEC mix, held through FY29); 3.2T ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 (HSBC via Exencial, relay [src 66]); top two end customers 33% + 28% [src 11].
drivers.derivation: Base (0.6814 - 0.04494 x 0.65) / 0.95506 = 68.29%. Actual quarters solved from the reported blended non-GAAP GM with optical at 65% (Q1 FY27 68.0% on optical 35.0 and copper 444.0 -> copper (0.680 x 479.0 - 0.65 x 35.0) / 444.0 = 68.24%; fifth gate fix, was 68.39% on the 55 / 424 split). FY27 (Q2-Q4): held at the Q1 FY27 68.24%: the blended margin stayed in 67.6-68.6% across the last five reported quarters while revenue rose from $223.1M to $479.0M [src 16, 15, 14, 13, 10], the Q2 guide is 67-69% [src 10], and no competing 1.6T AEC silicon ships before MaxLinear's first revenue in 2027 [src 41]. FY28-29 (second gate fix 2026-11-16, replaces the Q1 level held flat): the real-world case is price pressure on 1.6T AECs once cables built on competing retimer silicon ship. Marvell's retimer chips sell 15-20% below Credo's to third parties per Semi Fundamental's secondhand channel feedback ('we heard' [src 43]; not a measured price) and MaxLinear's silicon goes to cable makers for one or two large US data centers [src 40]; the gap is on the chip, which is only part of a cable's cost, so the cable-level gap is smaller: Credo is assumed to cut 1.6T AEC prices by 7.5% (half the 15% low end of the chip gap; estimate, confidence low) where a second source exists. Contested share of copper revenue c_q = AEC share 0.90 x 1.6T share of AEC revenue (56% = TrendForce's 2027 1.6T share of pluggable optical transceiver revenue [src 42], used as a proxy for AECs, held through FY29 (fourth gate fix; was +2pt a quarter to 70%, which no source supported): HSBC has 3.2T at ~30% of high-speed transceiver units by 2028 [src 66, relay], see copper_share) x 0.61 (MaxLinear's one or two US data centers, taken as Credo's top two end customers, 33% + 28% [src 11, 40]). With costs unchanged, GM_q = (0.682365 - 0.075 c_q) / (1 - 0.075 c_q): 67.49% in every FY28-29 quarter (-0.75pt). Direction: the evidence points down (new competitors, chip-price gap) and none points up for FY28-29. Alternatives sized (all under 5%): no price response (68.24%) +0.76%; full 17.5% chip gap matched on the contested volume -1.07%; the 7.5% cut on all 1.6T volume -0.50%; the old mix rise to 70% (67.49% to 67.30%) -0.11% (engine, 2026-11-23 set, research target (12m) 209.34). IP licensing carries almost no cost: FY25 IP license cost of revenue $171K on IP license revenue $12,476K = 1.37% (FY24 $816K on $28,024K) (FY25 10-K statement of operations, R5 [src 30]), so its small share of copper revenue lifts the copper margin slightly; it is inside the solved base, not a separate input. Blended GM from the segments after dc_mor (engine, 2026-11-23 set on the NVDA 11-17 capex path [src 101]): FY27 66.6%, FY28 63.3%, FY29 63.2% (2026-11-17: 66.6% / 63.3% / 63.3%), with optics on the booked Coherent anchor (Kilian card 2026-11-16 17:36Z; revenue-weighted optical GM 59.2% / 56.8% / 57.1%) at 18% / 39% / 40% of revenue (replaces the blend on the superseded 65% optical margin).

drivers.source: CY2025 $16.5B: LightCounting's January 2026 forecast for AI-cluster Ethernet optics as quoted in POET Technologies' FY2025 Form 20-F ('$26 billion in 2026, up ~60% year-over-year from $16.5 billion in 2025') [src 31]; LightCounting's own page returns HTTP 403. Lightwave's 2026-03-10 write-up of the same report prints $8B for 2025 [src 33]; the base level cancels in revenue (optical_share is calibrated to it on FY27 revenue), so only the growth path moves value. Growth: LightCounting's October forecast for Ethernet optical transceivers, +120% for 2026 and +76% for 2027, declining to +20% by 2031 (Lightwave 2026-10-08 [src 32]), applied to the AI-cluster market; its January AI-cluster Ethernet optics figure was +60% for 2026 [src 31]: two different LightCounting series, not one forecast revised.
drivers.derivation: CY2026 16.5 x 2.20 = $36.3B; CY2027 36.3 x 1.76 = $63.888B; CY2028: LightCounting's optics-to-capex ratio (Kilian 2026-10-27 17:21Z, replacing the straight-line interpolation of growth rates): optics sales to the top five cloud providers were 2.7% of their capex in 2025 and 3.1% in 2026, rising to 4.1% by 2031 (Lightwave 2026-03-10 on LightCounting's 'Optics for AI Clusters' [src 33]); linear between 2026 and 2031 (+0.2pt a year) gives 3.3% in 2027 and 3.5% in 2028. CY2028 growth = (Big-4 capex 1,305.26 / 1,009.45, the shared path from the NVDA 2026-11-17 round [src 101]) x (3.5% / 3.3%) = 1.2930 x 1.0606 = 1.3714; 63.888 x 1.3714 = $87.62B (update 2026-11-23; was 1,359.36 / 1,013.88 = 1.3408 x 1.0606 = 1.4220, $90.85B on the NVDA 11-09 path [src 35]; before 2026-11-13 1,330/1,080 x 1.0606 = 1.306, $83.438B). Cross-check: the pluggable transceiver market grows from 60 million units in 2026 to 175 million by 2030 (CEO quoting market forecasters, Q1 FY27 call [src 22]), (175/60)^(1/4) - 1 = +30.7% a year in units. CY2026-27 keep LightCounting's published growth rates (+120%, +76%) because they are published figures; the same ratio method would give +57% for 2027 (1,080/733 x 3.3/3.1), so the 2027 step is the richer of the two. Fiscal/calendar alignment: Credo's FY n runs May n-1 to April n (FY2026 ended 2026-05-02), so 8 of its 12 months fall in CY n-1; FY n is paired with CY n-1 (FY26 = CY2025, FY27 = CY2026, FY28 = CY2027, FY29 = CY2028), (calendar arithmetic; the pairing is the nearest calendar year, not a stated lead). Variants (engine-sized on the 2026-11-23 set, research target (12m) 209.34, judgment_alternatives): CY2028 tied to Big-4 capex growth alone (1,305.26 / 1,009.45 = +29.3%, $82.61B on the NVDA 2026-11-17 path; was +34.1%, $85.66B) -1.40%; the straight-line interpolation of LightCounting growth rates (+62%, $103.5B) +4.46%; the pre-update ratio build ($83.438B) -1.17%; LightCounting's ~+20% a year long-run rate from the same report ($8B 2025 -> $20B 2030 [src 33]) applied to CY2027-28 ($43.6B / $52.4B) -16.80% (carded); the CEO-quoted pluggable-transceiver unit growth, 60M units 2026 -> 175M 2030 = +30.7% a year [src 22], applied to CY2027-28 ($47.44B / $62.01B; units, not dollars, so any change in price per unit is left out) -12.79% (carded). The two 2026 growth figures are different LightCounting series: +60% for AI-cluster Ethernet optics in the January vintage quoted by POET [src 31], +120% for Ethernet optical transceivers in the October forecast [src 32]; the set applies the newer transceiver rate to the AI-cluster market (estimate). Vintage gap: our CY2026 $36.3B (16.5 x 2.20, October vintage) is above the $26B for 2026 in LightCounting's January vintage as quoted by POET [src 31] (36.3 / 26 - 1 = +40%); the October +120% (transceiver series) is the newer figure, so it is used; on the January AI-cluster series FY27 optical revenue would not change (optical FY27 is built by product line, not from the TAM), only the base share. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): Each quarter carries its fiscal year's calendar-year LightCounting level; the within-year shape sits in optical_share. Actual quarters carry the same estimate.
drivers.flag: CY2026-27 growth are LightCounting's Ethernet-transceiver rates applied to the AI-cluster subset; CY2028 is the ratio method (cited 2026 and 2031 ratios, linear in between), not a published 2028 figure.

drivers.label: Credo's share of the optical TAM (optical revenue / optical_tam)
drivers.source: Fifth gate fix 2026-11-16: Q1 FY27 optical capped by the 10-Q (AEC products 'contributed over 90% of the increase in revenue' [src 11]). Base: FY2026 optical revenue ~$60M (estimate, segment base row: optical DSPs only, 10 / 12 / 17 / 21 a quarter) / $16.5B = 0.364%. FY27 built by product line (fourth gate fix 2026-11-16): Q1 FY27 brought 'record revenue' in optical DSPs and the 'first silicon photonics PIC revenue following the Dust Photonics acquisition'; the initial PIC wins are in 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, 'and we expect these products to ramp throughout the year'; ZF optics 'production shipments are underway' with 'additional customer ramps during fiscal 27 across both 800-gig and 1.6T'; '1.6T DSP revenue remains on track for later this fiscal year' (Q1 FY27 call [src 22]). ZF optics will be 'clearly our largest revenue contributor for our optical portfolio' with 'a very aggressive ramp in the second half' and 'even more than double or triple that the following year'; each of the three lines 'is going to grow more than 80% year over year' (Q4 FY26 call [src 61]). DustPhotonics: acquired 2026-05-28; no revenue since acquisition is disclosed and pro forma results were not presented because the effect was not material (Q1 FY27 10-Q [src 11]); its PICs are 'deployed in transceivers at leading hyperscale AI clusters' and it is fabless (April 2026 8-K [src 69]); all its wafers are fabricated at Tower Semiconductor [src 63]. Tower's silicon-photonics revenue: annualized Q2 2026 run rate above $680 million [src 68]; ~$240M in Q3 2026, a Q4 2026 run rate above $1.1 billion, and start capacity at 3x the Q3 2026 level by Q3 2027 (~$720M a quarter) [src 62]. DustPhotonics deal call (Quartr summary [src 53]): combined optical 'over $500 million' in FY2027, up to 3.21M contingent shares on financial milestones, no DustPhotonics revenue figure. Market: LightCounting +120% for 2026 Ethernet transceivers, +76% for 2027 [src 32]. Credo's ramp record: FY25 quarterly revenue 59.8 / 72.0 / 135.0 / 170.0 during the AEC ramp (FY25 10-K and releases [src 30, 20, 19, 18]). Company plan (guidance_check only): 'more than $600 million of optical revenue in fiscal 27', each line 'more than $100 million' [src 22, 61]. FY28: dated additions (two next-generation design-win ramps, ALC initial revenue, NPO design wins) [src 22]. FY29: Marvell to acquire Lumentum, close expected H1 CY2028 [src 45]; HyperFrame Research's Ron Westfall sees the deal disrupting Marvell's neutrality and pushing merchant transceiver makers to hedge against lock-in, and Light Reading notes customer conflict, neither with a quantified share effect [src 64, 65]. Optical rebuild 2026-11-16 evidence: ZF optics 'three digit ASPs' vs 'two digit' for DSPs and PICs [src 61]; CEO: 'I have indicated previously that by the end of this fiscal year, we will be producing hundreds of thousands of units per month', to 'double and then even triple by the end of fiscal year 2028' (Goldman Sachs conference 2026-09-10, in answer to a question on the growth rate 'specifically for optics'; the CEO does not name the product [src 70]); Benzinga's June 2026 report of Credo's plan: 'Credo plans to ship hundreds of thousands of ZF transceiver units per month by late fiscal 2027', with 'a two to three-times volume ramp over the subsequent years' [src 76]; 'transceiver production' (Shareholders Unite, opinion [src 72]); CFO at the same conference: 'We guided about 11% sequentially into Q2', then 'call it 20% into Q3, 30% into Q4' for total revenue [src 70]; ZF customers: TensorWave in production, three more in qualification, 'more than 4' ramping in FY27, ramp pulled in to Q1 FY27 [src 71]; 1.6T ZF module with Credo's 224G DSP and Kfir200 PIC; Cignal AI 1.6T units >11M in 2026 and more than double in 2027 [src 73]; 800G module ~$400, 1.6T ~$1,300-1,500 [src 74]; 20-30% annual price erosion per speed class (the Highwater analyst's own view, not an AAOI statement [src 75]); Q1 FY27 10-Q: AEC products 'over 90% of the increase in revenue', inventory +$61.5M 'to support unfulfilled backlog and related new product ramps', DustPhotonics purchase price allocation: intangible assets $361.7M in one total (no split by type; the 10-Q's $15.0M customer-relationships line is a company-wide Note 6 figure, not tied to DustPhotonics), inventory $4.6M, contingent consideration $310M ($10.0M liability, $300.0M equity) [src 11]; up to ~3.21M contingent shares on financial milestones (April 2026 8-K [src 69]).
drivers.derivation: Fifth gate fix 2026-11-16 (replaces the optical rebuild's Q1 FY27 split of 55 and its wording that Credo stated a ZF unit rate). (1) Q1 FY27 split within the 10-Q cap: revenue rose $255.9M y/y (479.0 vs 223.1) and AEC products 'contributed over 90% of the increase in revenue' (Q1 FY27 10-Q [src 11]), so the non-AEC rise was under 0.10 x 255.9 = $25.6M; on the set's Q1 FY26 optical of 10, Q1 FY27 optical is at most ~35.6 (with the other non-AEC lines, IP and services, flat: the FY26 10-K has non-AEC revenue nearly flat over FY26 [src 12]). Booked 35.0 (estimate; AEC products 'contributed over 90% of the increase in revenue' (Q1 FY27 10-Q [src 11]) puts it below the 35.6 bound): optical DSPs 25.6 ('record revenue' [src 22]; FY26 base x1.2179) + SiPh PICs 5.0 (the 'first silicon photonics PIC revenue following the Dust Photonics acquisition' [src 22]; the acquisition closed on May 28, 2026, Q1 FY27 10-Q Note 5 [src 11]) + ZF optics 4.4 (the residual: 11.0k modules at $400; production shipments 'underway' [src 22]). Copper Q1 = 479.0 - 35.0 = 444.0. (2) What the CEO's 'units' are: at the Goldman Sachs conference (2026-09-10), asked how investors should think about the growth rate 'specifically for optics', the CEO said 'I have indicated previously that by the end of this fiscal year, we will be producing hundreds of thousands of units per month and then we will increase that production rate to double and then even triple by the end of fiscal year 2028' [src 70]; he does not name the product there, and the Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 call transcripts carry no unit rate [src 61, 22]. The earlier statement he refers to was reported by Benzinga in June 2026 as Credo's plan for ZF transceivers: 'Credo plans to ship hundreds of thousands of ZF transceiver units per month by late fiscal 2027', with 'a two to three-times volume ramp over the subsequent years' [src 76]; Shareholders Unite (opinion) also reads it as 'transceiver production' [src 72]. The merchant-chip reading fits the words less well: at the set's own DSP line (Q1 FY27 $25.6M at two-digit ASPs) Credo already ships on the order of a hundred thousand or more DSPs a month, so a rate the CEO gives as a year-end target and then doubles is a ramp of the new product. The ZF reading is therefore the set's estimate on a named outlet's report of Credo's plan (confidence medium), not a figure Credo states in its own transcripts; the reading in which 'units' counts all optical units is sized below (ZF from its own '>$100M' line, -31.34% / -27.72%, carded). (3) ZF-specific evidence the units build must also fit: ZF optics are complete transceivers at 'three digit' ASPs against 'two digit' for DSPs and PICs, ZF 'clearly our largest revenue contributor for our optical portfolio', each line 'more than $100 million' in FY27, 'a very aggressive ramp in the second half' and 'even more than double or triple that the following year' (Q4 FY26 call [src 61]); ZF customers: TensorWave in production, three more in qualification, 'more than 4' ramping in FY27, ramp pulled in to Q1 FY27 [src 71]; 'additional customer ramps during fiscal 27 across both 800-gig and 1.6T' [src 22]; the 1.6T ZF module carries Credo's own 224G DSP and Kfir200 PIC [src 73], so module revenue does not overlap the merchant DSP and PIC lines. DustPhotonics brings little revenue of its own: pro forma results not presented as not material, its intangibles booked as one $361.7M total, inventory $4.6M at the close, contingent consideration $310M (Q1 FY27 10-Q [src 11]; up to ~3.21M shares on financial milestones, April 2026 8-K [src 69]); its CEO on its earlier transceivers: 'We shipped thousands, not hundreds of thousands' [src 63]. FY27 by line: (a) optical DSPs: the FY26 base at LightCounting's +120% 2026 rate (x1.2179 a quarter [src 32]): 25.6 / 31.2 / 37.9 / 46.2 = $140.9M (1.6T DSP revenue later in FY27 left out). (b) SiPh PICs: Q1 ~$5M for the two months after the close, then a constant share of Tower Semiconductor's silicon-photonics output, DustPhotonics' sole foundry [src 62, 63, 68]: 5.0 / 10.6 / 12.1 / 18.7 = $46.4M (below the stated '>$100M'). (c) ZF optics = units x ASP. ASP $400 a module, the 800G market price [src 74], inside Credo's 'three digit' [src 61], with no ZeroFlap premium and no 1.6T mix (1.6T modules ~$1,300-1,500 [src 74]). Units rise at a constant monthly rate (x1.50 a month) from the capped Q1 (11.0k) to 200k a month in April 2027, the smallest reading of 'hundreds of thousands' at the year end [src 70, 76]: 11.0k / 37.1k / 125.2k / 422.3k units = $4.4M / $14.8M / $50.1M / $168.9M = $238.2M, above the stated '>$100M' and the largest of the three lines, as management says [src 61]. FY27 optical = 35.0 / 56.6 / 100.1 / 233.8 = $425.5M; share 425.5 / 36,300 = 1.172%; 29.1% below the company's '>$600M' (guidance_check: below). FY28: ZF units double over the year at a constant monthly rate to 400k a month by April 2028, the lower reading of 'double and then even triple' [src 70] and of Benzinga's 'two to three-times volume ramp' [src 76]: 674.2k / 801.8k / 953.5k / 1,133.9k = 3,563k units; ASP falls 25% a year from $400 (x0.9306 a quarter: $372 / $346 / $322 / $300), the middle of the Highwater analyst's '20% to 30% annual price erosion per speed class' (the author's own view, not an AAOI statement [src 75]), with no credit for the 1.6T mix: ZF $251.0M / $277.7M / $307.4M / $340.2M = $1,176.3M. That is 4.9x FY27 ZF revenue because FY27 is back-loaded (1.7x the Q4 FY27 exit run-rate of $675.6M a year, 5.4x the FY27 H2); management's 'even more than double or triple that the following year' [src 61] is a floor on the step, and the 2x and 3x readings on revenue are sized below. DSPs + PICs at the FY27 share of LightCounting's market (+76% [src 32]) = $329.6M, at a constant quarterly rate from the Q4 FY27 exit: 71.3 / 78.2 / 85.9 / 94.3. FY28 optical 322.2 / 356.0 / 393.3 / 434.5 = $1,505.9M (share 2.357%); the FY28 additions management dates without sizes (PIC next-generation design wins, ALC first revenue, NPO [src 22]) are left out. FY29: ZF units grow at the CEO-quoted pluggable-transceiver unit forecast, 60M in 2026 to 175M in 2030, +30.7% a year [src 22], from the 400k-a-month FY28 exit (1,255.0k / 1,341.8k / 1,434.7k / 1,534.0k = 5,566k units), ASP still -25% a year ($279 / $260 / $242 / $225): $1,391.0M; DSPs + PICs with the market (+37.1%, 87.62 / 63.888, the optics-to-capex build on the NVDA 2026-11-17 capex path [src 101]; was +42.2%, 90.85 / 63.888) = $452.1M at a constant quarterly rate from the Q4 FY28 exit (101.2 / 108.7 / 116.8 / 125.4; was $468.8M); FY29 optical 451.6 / 457.3 / 463.6 / 470.5 = $1,843.0M (share 2.104%; was 453.0 / 460.4 / 468.6 / 477.7 = $1,859.8M, share 2.047%). No Marvell-Lumentum socket loss is booked: the coverage found gives no quantified share effect [src 45, 64, 65]. After dc_mor: $425.5M / $1,450.0M / $1,829.5M (FY29 was $1,844.6M). Is it conservative (point checked 2026-11-16): each ZF reading is at its low or middle end (200k exit, doubling not tripling, -25% erosion where the market's blended price per unit falls an estimated ~17% from CY2026 to CY2027 (estimate, confidence low: LightCounting's +76% 2027 dollar growth for Ethernet optical transceivers [src 32] over HSBC's high-speed transceiver units, ~75m in 2026e to ~159m in 2027e, x2.12 [src 66]: 1.76 / 2.12 = 0.830, i.e. -17.0%; two different series and scopes, and the blended figure includes the 800G-to-1.6T mix shift, so per-speed erosion is steeper), no 1.6T mix) and FY27 total revenue $2,370.1M is 5.2% below Zacks' $2.50B [src 28]; but FY28 revenue before the moratorium haircut is $3,806.5M, 0.4% above Zacks' $3.79B (the 2026-11-23 nasdaq_est.py pull shows the same $3.79B), and $3,667.5M after it (-3.2%) (2026-11-23, NVDA 11-17 capex path [src 101]; was $2,372.7M, $3,845.4M (+1.5%) and $3,703.3M (-2.3%)). So the build is moderately conservative on its inputs and below Street for FY27, at Street for FY28 before dc_mor; it is not conservative against Street in FY28. No input is lowered to change that: the evidence on ASP and mix points up, not down (sized below). Cross-checks only (not inputs): FY27 total revenue $2,370.1M (+77.5%) vs the '>85%' guide [src 22] and Zacks' $2.50B [src 28]; FY28 $3,667.5M after dc_mor vs Zacks' $3.79B [src 28]; the CFO's ~+11% into Q2, ~+20% into Q3 and ~+30% into Q4 for total revenue [src 70] vs the build's +11.0%, +12.8% and +26.6% (was +13.0% / +26.8% before the 2026-11-23 capex-path update). Alternatives sized (engine, 2026-11-23 set, research target (12m) 209.34, judgment_alternatives): ZF from its own '>$100M' line with FY28 at 2x -31.34% and 3x -27.72%; ZF at the smallest 'largest line' level (= DSPs) with FY28 2.5x -26.68%; the FY25 AEC-ramp shape from the capped Q1 -34.84%; ZF FY28 at 2x FY27 revenue -24.05%; units triple by FY28 end +15.91%; exit 300k a month +18.25%; ASP held at $400 +14.09%; ZF mix at HSBC's 1.6T unit share +36.80% (all carded); the market's blended ASP path (-17% a year) +4.44%; the >$600M floor read +0.55%; the April 'greater than $500 million' +0.24%; the ZF H2 a quarter later -0.64%; PICs at $100M +2.86%; FY29 ZF units flat -1.43%; Marvell-Lumentum -15% on FY29 -3.69%; LightCounting's ~+20% a year market -16.80% and the CEO-quoted +30.7% unit growth -12.79% (optical_tam card). QUARTERS: share_q = optical revenue_q x 4 / (year TAM x 1000); FY26 optical 10 / 12 / 17 / 21 (estimate, DSPs only).

drivers.label: Largest end customer's share of revenue (end-customer basis), as a concentration term
drivers.source: FY2026 10-K end-customer table: Customer D 33%, Customer B 32%, Customer E 19% (direct-billing basis Customer A 49%) [src 12]. Q1 FY27 10-Q end-customer table: D 33%, C 28%, E 13%, F 10% (direct basis A 43%, 57% of receivables) [src 11]; CFO: 'our largest customer was a third of our revenue at 33%' [src 22].
drivers.derivation: Base 0.33 (FY26) and held at 0.33 in FY27-29 (Q1 FY27 33%; management expects 3-4 customers above 10% [src 22], i.e. diversification comes through the other customers, which the shares carry). Formula: each segment's revenue = TAM x share x 1000 x (1 - 0.33) / (1 - top_customer_pct). At the base path the factor is 1. Moving the driver to T means the top customer buys less (or more) while every other customer stays as the TAM x share build says: total revenue scales by 0.67 / (1 - T) and the top customer's revenue by T x 0.67 / (0.33 x (1 - T)). Bear: T 0.33 -> 0.21 cuts total revenue 15.2% and the top customer's revenue 46% (a 1.6T AEC dual-source to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices, agents 1-5). The top customer's product mix is not disclosed; the term applies to copper and optical alike (the CFO says these hyperscalers buy more than AECs [src 22]). Variant view: on the direct-billing basis (43%) the same customer-loss story is larger; the end-customer basis is used because the sourcing decision is the end customer's. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): 0.33 every quarter: FY26 10-K end-customer D 33% (the FY figure is used for each FY26 quarter: an annual concentration figure applied to each base quarter, so the base quarters aggregate to the 10-K's 0.33; the 10-Q end-customer tables give the quarter's largest end customer at 35% Q1 (acc 0001807794-25-000021), 42% Q2 (0001628280-25-054549), 39% Q3 (0001628280-26-014017), Q4 not disclosed, with the letters rotating between filings, so the quarter tops are not the FY top); Q1 FY27 10-Q D 33% [src 11]; held forward. The term is 1 at 0.33, so it moves revenue only in scenarios.
drivers.why: Concentration: one hyperscaler is a third of revenue; the agents' main bear story is its sourcing decision.

bull.story: Agents 1-5 bull (probabilities 0.22-0.25; values $345-380): Amazon Trn3 ramps strongly, Microsoft/Meta/Oracle and neoclouds broaden the base (3-4 customers >10%), optics pass a $1B run-rate, ALC/OmniConnect start; hyperscaler 2027 capex ~$1.2-1.3T. Restated: optical_share +15% (FY28 optical ~$1.4B), copper_share +5% (Credo holds 1.6T share), top_customer_pct +0.02 (Trn3: that customer +10%, total +3.1%), copper_tam and optical_tam +10%, gm +0.5pt both; P/E +3.5 turns to 27x.

guidance_check.why: Built by product line, not set at the floor (the >$600M is a cross-check only): $425.5M is 29.1% below the company's 'more than $600 million' [src 22]. Fifth gate fix: the 10-Q caps Q1 FY27 optical at ~35.6 (AEC products 'over 90% of the increase in revenue' [src 11]; the phrase is confirmed in that 10-Q by SEC full-text search [src 94]), so Q1 is 35.0 (was 55) and the ZF ramp starts from 4.4 (11.0k modules), which takes $126M out of FY27 ZF while the FY27 exit rate, and so FY28-29, are unchanged. ZF optics are complete transceivers at 'three digit' ASPs against two-digit DSPs and PICs [src 61]; the CEO gave a year-end rate of 'hundreds of thousands of units per month' without naming the product [src 70], which Benzinga reported in June as Credo's plan for 'ZF transceiver units' [src 76]; more than four ZF customers ramp in FY27 [src 71]. Why it lands below the floor: the Q1 start is capped, the exit rate is read at its smallest (200k a month), the module price at the 800G market $400 with no ZeroFlap premium or 1.6T mix [src 74], and the PIC line ($46.4M) at its foundry's output ramp because DustPhotonics brings little revenue of its own (pro forma results not material [src 11]). Against it: management has said '>$600M' twice, raised from 'greater than $500 million' in April [src 69, 22, 61], and beat all 8 first quarterly revenue guides (median +10.4%). The floor read for FY27 is +0.55%; the readings that move the target are FY28-29 (engine, 2026-11-23 set): ZF from its own '>$100M' line -31.34% (2x) / -27.72% (3x), the AEC-ramp shape -34.84%, ZF FY28 at 2x revenue -24.05%, exit 300k a month +18.25%, units triple +15.91%, ASP held +14.09%, HSBC 1.6T mix +36.80% (all carded). inputs_detail.derivation: PLAIN READING (Kilian 2026-11-16 16:15Z): copper revenue grows with Big-4 capex; this is not a market share. The 0.60% attach is a scaling device with no source: share is calibrated to Credo's actual copper revenue, so the attach level cancels and copper revenue = Q1 FY27 copper x capex growth x (1 - MaxLinear loss). No current public AEC market forecast was found: LightCounting's December 2023 newsletter put AOC, DAC and AEC sales at $2.8B by 2028 (stale, src 97); its December 2025 update is a paid report ($5,995, no figures on the public page, src 98), and 650 Group's AEC report publishes no figure in its launch release (src 99). Update 2026-11-13 (tape-hold read-through, 2026-11-16): capex path moved to the shared NVDA 11-09 hs_capex so every AI-capex name reads one path. TAM = Big-4 capex x 0.60%: CY2025 410 x 0.006 = $2.46B; CY2026 750.70 x 0.006 = $4.504B; CY2027 1,013.88 x 0.006 = $6.083B; CY2028 1,359.36 x 0.006 = $8.156B (was 4.398 / 6.48 / 7.98). Update 2026-11-23: the shared path moves to the NVDA 2026-11-17 print round's hs_capex [src 101] (per-company capacity build; Meta CY2028 199.8 = its CY2027 level, Kilian's NVDA card; the 11-09 path had Meta 2028 on its 2027 revenue growth a second year, refused there as a carried rate): CY2027 1,009.45 x 0.006 = $6.0567B, CY2028 1,305.26 x 0.006 = $7.8316B (was $6.083B / $8.156B); CY2026 750.70 unchanged. The 0.60% attach is a calibration: it makes Credo's FY2026 copper revenue (~$1,275M, see segment base) ~52% of the TAM; MaxLinear's CEO estimated that Credo accounts for 93% to 99% of the AEC cable market (Stocktwits' paraphrase of the call [src 40]), and Marvell retimers are the most widely adopted by AEC integrators [src 43], so Credo's share of the wider copper wallet (AECs plus retimers/PHYs) is below its AEC share. Cross-check: LightCounting puts optics sales to the top five cloud providers at 2.7% of their capex in 2025 (Lightwave 2026-03-10 on the 'Optics for AI Clusters' report [src 33]), so copper at 0.6% is ~1/5 of the optics spend (0.6 / 2.7 = 0.22). inputs_detail.derivation: Base 0.33 (FY26) and held at 0.33 in FY27-29 (Q1 FY27 33%; management expects 3-4 customers above 10% [src 22], i.e. diversification comes through the other customers, which the shares carry). Formula: each segment's revenue = TAM x share x 1000 x (1 - 0.33) / (1 - top_customer_pct). At the base path the factor is 1. Moving the driver to T means the top customer buys less (or more) while every other customer stays as the TAM x share build says: total revenue scales by 0.67 / (1 - T) and the top customer's revenue by T x 0.67 / (0.33 x (1 - T)). Bear: T 0.33 -> 0.21 cuts total revenue 15.2% and the top customer's revenue 46% (a 1.6T AEC dual-source to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices, agents 1-5). The top customer's product mix is not disclosed; the term applies to copper and optical alike (the CFO says these hyperscalers buy more than AECs [src 22]). Variant view: on the direct-billing basis (43%) the same customer-loss story is larger; the end-customer basis is used because the sourcing decision is the end customer's. QUARTERS (2026-10-29): 0.33 every quarter: FY26 10-K end-customer D 33% (the FY figure is used for each FY26 quarter: an annual concentration figure applied to each base quarter, so the base quarters aggregate to the 10-K's 0.33; the 10-Q end-customer tables give the quarter's largest end customer at 35% Q1 (acc 0001807794-25-000021), 42% Q2 (0001628280-25-054549), 39% Q3 (0001628280-26-014017), Q4 not disclosed, with the letters rotating between filings, so the quarter tops are not the FY top); Q1 FY27 10-Q D 33% [src 11]; held forward. The term is 1 at 0.33, so it moves revenue only in scenarios.
